title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
summary: The study reports XGBoost prediction of postoperative bleeding in separate MIMIC-IV and eICU cohorts, while noting that prospective timing validation is needed.
ai_technology: XGBoost predicts postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding from perioperative clinical variables.
organization: Department of Cardiovascular Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, China

evidence.tested: XGBoost was evaluated for postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding in separate MIMIC-IV and eICU cohorts; the source notes prospective timing validation is still needed.
evidence.unknown: External replication and real-world or clinical benefit were not established by the reviewed study
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost predicts postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding from perioperative clinical variables.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
